extracted.intended_audience: architects, architecture students, and educated readers interested in Gothic architecture
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting the moral, aesthetic, and formal criteria that Ruskin uses to define and evaluate Gothic architecture — its spirit (naturalism, humility, grotesque, rigidity, etc.) and its formal rules (pointed arch for roof proper; gable for roof-mask; scale-invariant grouping).

rubrics_metrics.name: Humility / confession_of_imperfection
rubrics_metrics.description: Humility which confesses the imperfection of the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Christian/Gothic workman 'freely confesses both, and neither seeks to disguise his own roughness of work, nor his subject's roughness of make.' Humility is part of the Gothic spirit: frankness joined with depth of religious feeling and charity. This humility appears in accumulation of ornament that admits the work of many hands and addresses both rude and refined minds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veracity / faithful_portraiture
rubrics_metrics.description: Veracity of portraiture: 'never so as to lose the veracity of portraiture... not exalting its kings into demi-gods, nor its saints into archangels, but giving what kingliness and sanctity was in them, to the full, mixed with due record of their faults.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gothic sculpture and painting include minute and general delineation and introduce familiar scenes and simple subjects (domestic customs, inferior arts). The work should record virtues and errors with 'unmoved and unexcusing resoluteness,' leaving the reader to form his own estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalism / fondness_for_vegetation
rubrics_metrics.description: The peculiar fondness for the forms of vegetation: the living foliage became a subject of intense affection and was rendered with as much accuracy as compatible with design and material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vegetation is not merely accessory but treated as a separate subject; Gothic workmen struggled to render foliage's characters, sometimes transgressing the laws of design and material in enthusiasm. This choice indicates higher civilization and a gentler temperament; delicate observation of vegetation signals rural, thoughtful life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense_of_the_grotesque
rubrics_metrics.description: A tendency to delight in fantastic and ludicrous, as well as in sublime, images: 'the sense of the Grotesque' is a universal instinct of the Gothic imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ruskin defers precise definition but insists readers familiar with Gothic will recognise the propensity to include fantastic/ludicrous imagery alongside sublime forms; it is an essential element of the Gothic mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigidity (active_rigidity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Active rigidity: not merely stable but 'active rigidity' — energy giving tension to movement and stiffness to resistance, making forms angular rather than curved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This character is expressed throughout Gothic structure and decoration: vaults, traceries, ornament that 'stands out in prickly independence, and frosty fortitude,' jutting into crockets, pinnacles, alternately thorny or bossy. It errs on the side of brusquerie rather than languor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workmanship_habits_and_material_influence
rubrics_metrics.description: The habits of hard and rapid working, industry, and the influence of a rougher material contribute to Gothic characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Northern climate and livelihood (cold, winter life) produce a taste that finds pleasure in 'leafless' or 'checked by cold' vegetation forms and in crisp, angular expression. Rough materials compel seeking vigor of effect over refinement of texture or accuracy of form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance_of_elements / measure_vs_excess
rubrics_metrics.description: There is virtue in the measure and error in the excess of Gothic characters; the best architecture unites opposing qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While Gothic admits frankness, changefulness, and naturalism, it 'may go too far in its rigidity' and 'lose itself either in frivolity of division, or perversity of purpose.' The best Gothic balances northern energy with southern grace; excess of any single impulse is a fault.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundance / decorative_accumulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Redundance — the uncalculating bestowal of the wealth of labor (accumulation of ornament) — is a constituent element of Gothic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although some Gothic depends on simple design, characteristic buildings often rely on ornamental accumulation to achieve effect. This richness addresses both the rudest and the most refined minds and is paradoxically part of Gothic humility (allowing co-operation of many hands). It also stems from enthusiasm and sympathy with the profusion of nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gothic_is_gradational
rubrics_metrics.description: A building is more or less Gothic in proportion to the number of Gothic forms it unites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ruskin asserts we cannot simply call a building Gothic or not; degree depends on presence of Gothic forms. Some elements may be missing in particular examples; purity is a matter of proportion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pointed_arch_for_roof_proper
rubrics_metrics.description: "Gothic architecture is that which uses, if possible, the pointed arch in the roof proper."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the first formal clause of definition: the pointed arch should be the principal form adopted either in the stone vaulting or the timbers of the roof proper. Exceptions are allowed when necessary for domestic requirements (e.g., flat ceilings when whole apartment height is required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gable_for_roof_mask
rubrics_metrics.description: "Gothic architecture is that which uses the pointed arch for the roof proper, and the gable for the roof-mask."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cold, wet climates the gable is the advisable form for the roof-mask because it throws off rain and snow. Ruskin treats the gable as a far more essential feature of Northern architecture than the pointed vault; the gable (roof-mask) is often the decisive Gothic sign for houses and domestic buildings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roof_proper_vs_roof_mask_distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Roofs are divided into the roof proper (shell/vault/ceiling, internally visible) and the roof-mask (which protects the lower roof from weather); they can be independent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some Gothic buildings have a flat or domed roof proper while their walls use pointed arches; these may still be Gothic in spirit. But as concerns roofing alone, a structure is not Gothic unless the pointed arch is principal in the roof proper. The gable for roof-mask is less excusable to abandon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wilful_transgression_of_law_is_corrupting
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is not the compelled, but the wilful transgression of law which corrupts the character."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If departures from Gothic law are necessary (compelled by space or material) they do not necessarily corrupt Gothic purity; but wilful, capricious use of non-Gothic forms (e.g., domes, Turkish or Chinese roofs as roof-masks) 'the building has positive corruption mingled with its Gothic elements' and 'the Gothic has lost its character.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Gable_weight_over_pointed_windows
rubrics_metrics.description: A house with square windows but a boldly gabled roof is more Gothic than one with pointed windows but a domed or flat roof-mask.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical construction often forces square lintels in small work; such features do not 'un-Gothicize' a building so long as the bold gable roof is retained and the spirit of the work remains Gothic. The roof-mask form can outweigh window arch shape in determining Gothic character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale-invariance_of_gothic_group
rubrics_metrics.description: All good Gothic is the development, on every scale, of the group formed by the pointed arch below and the gable above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the cathedral roof and vaults to the smallest niche point, the single law of the gable over the pointed arch appears repeatedly. Gothic character depends on these primary lines endlessly rearranged or repeated; the modes of support and decoration vary, but the pointed-arch + gable group defines the style.
